'''Ulf Hohmann''' (born 9 July 1963, in [[Stuttgart]]) is a German [[Ethology|ethologist]], whose studies about the [[raccoon]] have played a significant role in the understanding of its [[social behavior]] and its distribution in Germany.

== Biography ==

Studying at the universities [[University of Tübingen]] and [[University of Kiel]], Ulf Hohmann completed his [[diploma]] of [[Biology]] in 1992.<ref name="gwn">{{cite web | url=http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/ulfenglisch.html | title=Forum: Dr. Ulf Hohmann | accessdate=2008-07-26 | work=GWN-Homepage | publisher=Gesellschaft für Wildökologie und Naturschutz e.V. | archive-date=2008-03-29 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080329033545/http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/ulfenglisch.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> After the submission of his [[dissertation]] to [[Antal Festetics]] at the forestal faculty of the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1998,<ref name="gwn" /> he was the chairperson of the ''Gesellschaft für Wildökologie und Naturschutz e.V.'' (''Society for wildlife ecology and conservation e.V.'').<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/frame8.htm | title=Presseinfos | accessdate=2008-07-26 | date=2001-04-20 | work=GWN-Homepage | publisher=Gesellschaft für Wildökologie und Naturschutz e.V. | language=German | archive-date=2008-03-21 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080321053213/http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/frame8.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref> In this role, he appeared in the media as expert for the increasing urbanisation of animals.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/publicationlist.html | title=Forum: Weitere Veröffentlichungen | accessdate=2008-07-26 | work=GWN-Homepage | publisher=Gesellschaft für Wildökologie und Naturschutz e.V. | language=German | archive-date=2008-03-29 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080329033540/http://www.gwn.de/gwn/html/publicationlist.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> At the moment (July 2008), he works for the ''Forschungsanstalt für Waldökologie und Forstwirtschaft Rheinland-Pfalz'' (''Research institute for forest ecology and forestry Rhineland-Palatinate'') located in [[Trippstadt]].<ref name="fwf">{{cite web | url=http://www.wald-rlp.de/index.php?id=3124&user_projects_pi1=21 | title=Hohmann, Dr. Ulf | accessdate=2008-07-26 | year=2005 | work=Landesforsten Rheinland-Pfalz | language=German }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

== Research ==

Within the scope of his dissertation, Ulf Hohmann and several scientific assistants carried out the first systematic study of the German raccoon population from 1992 to 1998.<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 24–25</ref> The [[telemetry|telemetric]] measurement of the movement patterns of the raccoons living in the [[Lower Saxony]] low mountain range [[Solling]] yielded the result that the social behavior of raccoons is gender-specific and that they often live together in small, loose groups instead of being [[loner]]s like previously thought.<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 155</ref> Stanley D. Gehrt arrived at the same conclusion in his study done in [[Texas]] in 1994 one year after Hohmann's initial query to Gehrt's doctoral adviser and raccoon expert Erik Fritzell about his discoveries.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Gehrt | first=Stanley D. | title=Raccoon social organization in South Texas | year= 1994}} (Dissertation at the University of Missouri-Columbia)</ref><ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 30</ref> (→ [[Raccoon#Social behavior|Social behavior of raccoons]])

The study was supplemented with the observation of the behavior of several raised and subsequently released raccoon kits.<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 31–41</ref> This work, started by the graduand Franziska Kalz in 1995,<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 32</ref> was accompanied by the [[Wildlife photography|wildlife photographer]] Ingo Bartussek since spring 1996.<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 39</ref> Beginning in 1999, after the submission of his dissertation, Ulf Hohmann carried out the first study of urban raccoons outside of [[North America]] in the [[Hesse|Hessian]] small town [[Bad Karlshafen]].<ref>Hohmann (2001), p. 104–109</ref> In 2001, Ulf Hohmann published the [[monograph]] ''Der Waschbär'' (''The raccoon''), giving a thorough overview of appearance and behavior of the species and the results of his studies in it. Besides numerous photos of Ingo Bartussek, the book also contains a chapter about raising raccoon kits written by the [[veterinarian]] Bernhard Böer.

Working now for the ''Forschungsanstalt für Waldökologie und Forstwirtschaft Rheinland-Pfalz'', Ulf Hohmann has recently concentrated on the research of [[boar]]s, mainly of those living in the [[Palatinate Forest]].<ref name="fwf" /> His research on raccoons has been continued by Frank-Uwe Michler, who first worked together with Hohmann for his diploma in a study of urban raccoons in [[Kassel]] from 2001 to 2002.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.diewaschbaerenkommen.de/html/kassel.html | title=Die Ergebnisse des Forschungsprojektes "Untersuchungen zur Ökologie urbaner Waschbär-Vorkommen am Beispiel der Stadt Kassel" | accessdate=2008-07-26 | last=Bartussek | first=Ingo | work=Die Waschbären kommen | language=German}}</ref> Since March 2006, Frank-Uwe Michler is the leader of the first study of the range and behavior of the raccoons living in the eastern parts of Germany in the [[Müritz National Park]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.projekt-waschbaer.de/kontakt-und-ansprechpartner/ | title=Projektleitung / Ansprechpartner | accessdate=2008-07-26 | last=Michler | first=Frank-Uwe |author2=Köhnemann, Berit A. | work=„Projekt Waschbär“ | publisher=Gesellschaft für Wildökologie und Naturschutz e.V. | language=German}}</ref>
